title: E-Commerce Engine — Dashboard
description: Clean, simple monitoring dashboard for the e-commerce backend. Tracks HTTP traffic, background queues, Redis cache, database transactions, and load distribution across all app instances.

panels.title: Healthy Instances
panels.description: Shows how many of the 3 app instances are running and healthy. If this drops below 3, a server may have crashed. > This tests load balancing fault tolerance (Task 5).

panels.title: Request Rate
panels.description: Total API requests handled in the last 5 minutes across all app instances. Spikes indicate traffic bursts (e.g., load tests, flash sales). > Tracks overall system load (Tasks 1, 2, 5).

panels.title: Error Count
panels.description: Total HTTP errors (4xx client + 5xx server errors). Green = 0 errors. Yellow = some 4xx (expected with rate limiting). Red = 5+ errors (possible bugs). > 4xx = rate limiting (Task 2), 5xx = real failures.

panels.title: Avg Response Time
panels.description: Average response time across all API requests. Green = fast (<500ms). Yellow = slow (500ms-1s). Red = too slow (>1s). > Cached routes should be <100ms, async order dispatch <500ms (Tasks 3, 6).

panels.title: Queue Backlog
panels.description: Total pending jobs across all queues (default, invoices, notifications, analytics). Green = under 100. Yellow = 100-500. Red = over 500 (workers can't keep up). > Spikes mean orders are coming in faster than workers can process (Tasks 3, 4).

panels.title: Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description: Percentage of requests served from Redis cache vs hitting the database. Green = 95%+ (excellent). Yellow = 80-95%. Red = below 80% (cache miss storm). > Higher is better — it means the database is under less load (Task 6).

panels.title: Requests by Instance & Route
panels.description: HTTP request counts broken down by app instance (app1, app2, app3) and API route (products, orders, cart, etc.). > Helps identify which endpoints receive the most traffic and whether Nginx is distributing load correctly across all 3 servers (Task 5).

panels.title: Response Time by Route
panels.description: How long each API route takes to respond. Fast routes (<100ms) = cached products. Medium (100-500ms) = orders with async dispatch. Slow (>500ms) = something is blocking. > Cached product lists should be ~2ms, order placement with async dispatch should be ~50ms (Task 6).

panels.title: Errors by Status Code
panels.description: HTTP error counts broken down by status code and route. 4xx errors = client issues (rate limiting at 429, stock at 422). 5xx errors = server bugs. > High 429 counts = rate limiting is working (Task 2). High 422 = stock running out (Task 1).

panels.title: Rate-Limited Requests (429s)
panels.description: Requests that were rejected with HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests). Each spike means users hit the rate limit (10 orders/minute/user). > This confirms the rate limiting middleware is active and protecting the system from abuse (Task 2).

panels.title: Total Requests vs Errors Over Time
panels.description: Overlays total requests with total errors on the same timeline. Spikes in errors that match request spikes = rate limiting (expected behavior). Errors without corresponding requests = real server issues. > Green area = healthy traffic. Red spikes need investigation.

panels.title: Queue Depth by Queue
panels.description: Number of pending jobs waiting to be processed per queue. Queues: default (order processing), invoices, notifications, analytics. > If depth keeps growing, queue workers can't keep up. Healthy = 0-10 jobs pending (Tasks 3, 4).

panels.title: Cache Hit Ratio Over Time
panels.description: Cache efficiency over time. A hit ratio of 1.0 = every request is served from cache (fast). A drop to 0 = every request hits the database (slow). > Drops can mean: (1) cache TTL expired, (2) cache stampede (many requests miss simultaneously), or (3) cache was flushed after an inventory update (Task 6).

panels.title: Cache Hits vs Misses
panels.description: Raw counts of cache hits (data found in Redis) vs misses (data not found, fell through to database). Hits should far outnumber misses. > High miss counts = either cache TTL is too short, or the cache was recently flushed after product updates (Task 6).

panels.title: Database Queries by Type
panels.description: Database queries broken down by type (select, insert, update, delete). Select = product browsing (read-heavy). Insert/update = orders and inventory changes (write-heavy). > This helps identify if the system is read-heavy (many product views) or write-heavy (many orders).

panels.title: Committed vs Rolled Back Transactions
panels.description: Database transaction outcomes. 'committed' = order placed successfully. 'rolled_back' = something failed mid-checkout. > High rollback rates = lock contention (two users ordering the same product simultaneously — Task 1) or payment failures (card declined — Task 8).

panels.title: Slow Queries (>100ms)
panels.description: Queries that took more than 100ms to execute. Slow queries degrade API response times. Common causes: missing database indexes, N+1 query patterns, or lock waits from concurrent transactions (Task 1, Task 7). Note: with SQLite, queries are typically fast (<1ms) so this panel may show no data — that's expected and healthy.

panels.title: Traffic Share by Instance
panels.description: What percentage of total traffic each app instance handles. The Nginx load balancer is configured with a 3:2:1 weight ratio — app1 should get ~50%, app2 ~33%, app3 ~17%. > Note: all instances share the same Redis, so they report identical values. The Nginx weighted distribution IS working (proven by test scripts), but per-instance metrics would require per-instance Redis keys.

panels.title: Response Time by Instance
panels.description: Average response time per app instance. All 3 instances should have similar latency. If one instance is much slower, it may have resource contention (CPU/memory limits) or be processing heavier requests (Task 5).

panels.title: Total Requests Handled
panels.description: Total requests handled by each instance as a horizontal bar chart. Quickly compares load between app1 (should be highest at ~50%), app2 (~33%), and app3 (~17%) according to Nginx weights (Task 5).
